the study of mitochondrial DNA in Tunisian patients suffering from Leigh syndrome.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T5522G and A5558G mutations are associated with Leigh syndrome in Tunisian patients and that they may have a significant role in the pathogenesis of the disorder.
the two novel mutations in the tRNA(Leut) gene are the cause of Leigh syndrome.
mitochondrial tRNA mutations in the tRNA(Leucine), tRNA(Valine), tRNA(Serine) and tRNA(Trypophane) genes are the most frequent mutations in Tunisian LS patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two new mutations in the tRNA(Leucine) gene (T5523 G and A5559 G) are likely to be the cause of LS in our patients.
the two mutations described in the present study are the most frequent in the Tunisian patients and are the first reported in Tunisia and in Africa.
the mutations in the tRNA(Val) and tRNA(Trn) genes are responsible for the majority of the mitochondrial mutations in our patients with LS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondrial tRNA(TrP) is a hot-spot for pathogenic mutations.
the mitochondrial tRNA(Trps) gene could represent a new candidate gene involved in the pathogenesis of Leigh syndrome.
the screening of the mitochondrial genome is necessary in order to detect the mutations responsible for Leigh syndrome.
